children: SEMI and IDTA plan a national Semiconductor Academy focused on skills, training and employment across India's growing chip ecosystem

SEMI, the global semiconductor industry association, and the India Deep Tech Alliance have announced plans to collaborate on establishing the India Semiconductor Academy as a national, industry-led platform for semiconductor education, skills development and employment.
The proposed academy will focus on building an industry-ready workforce as India expands investments across semiconductor design, fabrication, advanced packaging and testing, equipment and materials.

SEMI and IDTA said the initiative will seek to connect India's engineering and technical talent with practical skills required across the semiconductor value chain. The proposed platform will work with industry participants and academic institutions, including Cadence, CG Semi, Dixon Technologies, Micron Technology, 3D Glass Solutions, the University of California San Diego and IIT Kanpur.

During the planning phase, SEMI and IDTA will consult semiconductor companies, universities, technical institutions, training centres and laboratories to develop the academy's governance structure, operating model, curriculum priorities, funding framework and implementation plan.

The proposed framework includes an annual forecast of semiconductor skills demand by role, capability and location, along with industry-validated occupational standards and stackable credentials for priority jobs. It will also cover access to laboratories, tools and simulation environments, apprenticeships, on-the-job training and employment-linked programmes.

The academy is intended to address workforce requirements across the talent pyramid, ranging from fab-ready technicians and operators to manufacturing, packaging and design engineers, researchers, materials scientists and system architects.

S Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, said the proposed academy could align education and skilling with industry requirements and create pathways from training to employment.

Ajit Manocha, President and Chief Executive Officer, SEMI, said the collaboration would focus on connecting educators, employers and learners through industry-defined competencies and hands-on training.

Arun Kumar, Chair of the Executive Committee at IDTA and Managing Partner at Celesta Capital, said workforce development would be a key requirement as India expands its semiconductor capabilities, with the proposed academy aimed at developing fab-ready and industry-ready skills.

The initiative is also expected to complement Pax Silica, a partnership involving India, the US and other countries focused on semiconductor and artificial intelligence supply-chain resilience and technology cooperation.

SEMI and IDTA will establish a joint working process and consult industry and academic partners before finalising the institutional design. The plan is expected to outline requirements including public support, industry contributions, access to facilities and expertise and long-term programme revenues.
